rubric: The external callus develops around the outside of the break.
Periosteal chondrocytes and osteoblasts contribute to its cartilage and bone.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Starting a callus at about 48 hours means the fracture is already fully healed.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: The chapter describes the start of callus formation within about 48 hours. These textbook intervals are approximate and do not mean healing is complete.
rubric: The chapter describes the start of callus formation within about 48 hours.
These textbook intervals are approximate and do not mean healing is complete.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Only final compact bone can provide any stabilization during repair.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: The repair calli bridge and surround the damaged region. Their formation provides stabilization while repair progresses.
rubric: The repair calli bridge and surround the damaged region.
Their formation provides stabilization while repair progresses.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The internal callus is mature compact bone from its first appearance.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Endosteal chondrocytes produce a fibrocartilaginous internal bridge. It is an early repair matrix that will subsequently be replaced by bone.
rubric: Endosteal chondrocytes produce a fibrocartilaginous internal bridge.
It is an early repair matrix that will subsequently be replaced by bone.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Only red marrow produces the external callus.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Periosteal chondrocytes produce hyaline cartilage. Periosteal osteoblasts contribute bone to the external collar.
rubric: Periosteal chondrocytes produce hyaline cartilage.
Periosteal osteoblasts contribute bone to the external collar.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The cartilage callus remains unchanged throughout fracture healing.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Trabecular bone replaces the callus cartilage. This replacement builds a bony bridge before later remodeling.
rubric: Trabecular bone replaces the callus cartilage.
This replacement builds a bony bridge before later remodeling.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Replacing cartilage with bone during repair is called blood coagulation.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Endochondral ossification replaces a cartilage framework with bone. This process occurs when repair callus cartilage becomes trabecular bone.
rubric: Endochondral ossification replaces a cartilage framework with bone.
This process occurs when repair callus cartilage becomes trabecular bone.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Osteoblasts are the principal cells that resorb dead bone.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Osteoclasts resorb old or damaged bone. Removing dead bone participates in the replacement and remodeling process.
rubric: Osteoclasts resorb old or damaged bone.
Removing dead bone participates in the replacement and remodeling process.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Osteogenic cells replenish the bone by becoming osteoclasts.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Osteogenic cells are bone-forming progenitors with mitotic activity. They differentiate into osteoblasts that contribute new bone.
rubric: Osteogenic cells are bone-forming progenitors with mitotic activity.
They differentiate into osteoblasts that contribute new bone.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The outer margins are permanently left as an unmineralized hematoma.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Later repair replaces spongy bone at the outer margins with compact bone. This change contributes to the restored outer structure.
rubric: Later repair replaces spongy bone at the outer margins with compact bone.
This change contributes to the restored outer structure.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Any slight swelling must remain permanently after a fracture heals.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Remodeling reshapes the repaired bone. It may remove much of the external evidence of the fracture.
rubric: Remodeling reshapes the repaired bone.
It may remove much of the external evidence of the fracture.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The internal and external calli never connect during healing.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Internal and external calli eventually unite. Their union contributes to a continuous repair bridge.
rubric: Internal and external calli eventually unite.
Their union contributes to a continuous repair bridge.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Final remodeling is the first major stage of fracture repair.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: The hematoma appears early after vessel damage. Internal and external calli follow the clotting stage.
rubric: The hematoma appears early after vessel damage.
Internal and external calli follow the clotting stage.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The early cartilage callus is immediately the final remodeled structure.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Callus cartilage is replaced by trabecular bone to make a bony callus. Later remodeling reshapes this bony repair region.
rubric: Callus cartilage is replaced by trabecular bone to make a bony callus.
Later remodeling reshapes this bony repair region.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Cartilage replacement after an adult fracture always means normal height growth has restarted.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Endochondral ossification can participate in fracture repair. Use of this mechanism does not mean an adult growth plate has reopened.
rubric: Endochondral ossification can participate in fracture repair.
Use of this mechanism does not mean an adult growth plate has reopened.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Osteoclast” to this prompt: Which bone cell forms new bone matrix? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Osteoblasts synthesize and secrete bone matrix components. They form bone rather than resorbing it.
rubric: Osteoblasts synthesize and secrete bone matrix components.
They form bone rather than resorbing it.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Osteoblast” to this prompt: Which bone cell resorbs old, injured, or unnecessary bone? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Osteoclasts carry out bone resorption. Their activity removes bone instead of depositing new matrix.
rubric: Osteoclasts carry out bone resorption.
Their activity removes bone instead of depositing new matrix.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Osteoclast” to this prompt: Which mature bone cell maintains the surrounding matrix? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Osteocytes are mature cells embedded in bone matrix. They help maintain mineral concentration in the matrix.
rubric: Osteocytes are mature cells embedded in bone matrix.
They help maintain mineral concentration in the matrix.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Osteocyte” to this prompt: Which undifferentiated bone cell can divide and produce osteoblasts? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Osteogenic cells have high mitotic activity. Their descendants differentiate into bone-forming osteoblasts.
rubric: Osteogenic cells have high mitotic activity.
Their descendants differentiate into bone-forming osteoblasts.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Osteoclast” to this prompt: An osteoblast becomes surrounded by the matrix it secreted. What cell does it become? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: An embedded osteoblast changes into an osteocyte. This conversion links matrix formation to mature matrix maintenance.
rubric: An embedded osteoblast changes into an osteocyte.
This conversion links matrix formation to mature matrix maintenance.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Osteogenic cells only” to this prompt: Which lineage supplies osteoclasts? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Osteoclasts arise from monocyte and macrophage lineages. They do not arise from the osteogenic-cell lineage that produces osteoblasts.
rubric: Osteoclasts arise from monocyte and macrophage lineages.
They do not arise from the osteogenic-cell lineage that produces osteoblasts.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Osteoblast” to this prompt: Which resorbing bone cell is multinucleated? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Osteoclasts have multiple nuclei. Their multinucleated structure accompanies their resorptive role.
rubric: Osteoclasts have multiple nuclei.
Their multinucleated structure accompanies their resorptive role.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Mature osteocytes” to this prompt: Which of the four main bone-cell categories retains mitotic activity? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: The chapter identifies osteogenic cells as the dividing bone-cell population. Mature osteoblasts and osteocytes do not replenish themselves by mitosis.
rubric: The chapter identifies osteogenic cells as the dividing bone-cell population.
Mature osteoblasts and osteocytes do not replenish themselves by mitosis.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Central canal” to this prompt: What small space houses an osteocyte? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: An osteocyte lies in a lacuna within the matrix. The lacuna is a cell-sized space rather than the shaft marrow cavity.
rubric: An osteocyte lies in a lacuna within the matrix.
The lacuna is a cell-sized space rather than the shaft marrow cavity.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Lacunae” to this prompt: Which small matrix channels allow osteocyte processes to communicate and obtain nutrients? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Canaliculi connect spaces through the bone matrix. Osteocyte processes extend through them for communication and nutrient exchange.
rubric: Canaliculi connect spaces through the bone matrix.
Osteocyte processes extend through them for communication and nutrient exchange.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “All callus cartilage is made by osteoclasts.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Chondrocytes associated with the endosteum form the internal repair matrix. Their product is fibrocartilage between the broken ends.
rubric: Chondrocytes associated with the endosteum form the internal repair matrix.
Their product is fibrocartilage between the broken ends.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The hyaline cartilage of the external callus is secreted by osteoclasts.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Periosteal chondrocytes contribute hyaline cartilage around the outside of the break. The external callus also receives bone from osteoblasts.
rubric: Periosteal chondrocytes contribute hyaline cartilage around the outside of the break.
The external callus also receives bone from osteoblasts.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “An external callus contains cartilage but never bone.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Periosteal osteoblasts deposit the bone component of the external callus. Chondrocytes contribute its cartilage component.
rubric: Periosteal osteoblasts deposit the bone component of the external callus.
Chondrocytes contribute its cartilage component.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Endosteum” to this prompt: Which membrane covers the outside of bone except at articular surfaces? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: The periosteum covers the external surface of bone. Its deeper layer contains cells involved in growth and repair.
rubric: The periosteum covers the external surface of bone.
Its deeper layer contains cells involved in growth and repair.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Periosteum” to this prompt: Which membrane lines the internal marrow cavity and other internal bone surfaces? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: The endosteum lines internal bone surfaces. It contains cells that participate in bone growth, remodeling, and repair.
rubric: The endosteum lines internal bone surfaces.
It contains cells that participate in bone growth, remodeling, and repair.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Hydroxyapatite crystals” to this prompt: Which matrix component gives bone flexibility rather than mineral hardness? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Collagen contributes flexibility to the matrix. Mineral crystals provide much of its hardness and strength.
rubric: Collagen contributes flexibility to the matrix.
Mineral crystals provide much of its hardness and strength.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Collagen” to this prompt: Which mineral crystals give bone much of its hardness? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Hydroxyapatite crystals mineralize the matrix. Their contribution differs from the flexibility provided by collagen fibers.
rubric: Hydroxyapatite crystals mineralize the matrix.
Their contribution differs from the flexibility provided by collagen fibers.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Reduction” to this prompt: What is the breakdown or removal of bone by osteoclasts called? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Resorption removes bone material. It occurs during remodeling and can release stored calcium.
rubric: Resorption removes bone material.
It occurs during remodeling and can release stored calcium.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Osteoclasts” to this prompt: Which cells secrete the collagen matrix and calcium salts during bone formation? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Osteoblasts synthesize and secrete matrix components. As their surrounding matrix calcifies, some become embedded osteocytes.
rubric: Osteoblasts synthesize and secrete matrix components.
As their surrounding matrix calcifies, some become embedded osteocytes.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Only articular cartilage” to this prompt: Where does the chapter locate immature osteogenic cells? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Osteogenic cells occur in deep periosteal layers and the marrow. Their location supplies progenitors for bone formation.
rubric: Osteogenic cells occur in deep periosteal layers and the marrow.
Their location supplies progenitors for bone formation.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Only inside osteocyte lacunae” to this prompt: Where are active osteoclasts found carrying out bone resorption? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Osteoclasts act at bone surfaces. They resorb old, injured, or unnecessary bone at those surfaces.
rubric: Osteoclasts act at bone surfaces.
They resorb old, injured, or unnecessary bone at those surfaces.

written.prompt: A learner answers “Permanent arrest of bone activity” to this prompt: What ongoing process combines osteoclast resorption with osteoblast formation? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Remodeling includes coordinated removal and formation of bone. The balance of these activities subtly reshapes living bone.
rubric: Remodeling includes coordinated removal and formation of bone.
The balance of these activities subtly reshapes living bone.

written.prompt: A learner answers “An inert solid with no cells” to this prompt: Which description of bone explains why it can remodel and repair itself? Explain the correct term and its function.
written.explanation: Bone contains living cells and a matrix. Its vascular supply and active cells support continual turnover.
rubric: Bone contains living cells and a matrix.
Its vascular supply and active cells support continual turnover.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The soft callus is already mature bone and needs no tissue replacement.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Repair cartilage is replaced with trabecular bone. Bone deposition follows the temporary cartilage stage rather than merely renaming it.
rubric: Repair cartilage is replaced with trabecular bone.
Bone deposition follows the temporary cartilage stage rather than merely renaming it.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The diaphysis is the expanded articular end of a long bone.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: The diaphysis forms the long shaft. Its central marrow cavity is surrounded by substantial compact bone.
rubric: The diaphysis forms the long shaft.
Its central marrow cavity is surrounded by substantial compact bone.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Epiphysis refers to the membrane lining the marrow cavity.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: An epiphysis is an expanded end of a long bone. Spongy bone lies within it beneath an outer compact layer.
rubric: An epiphysis is an expanded end of a long bone.
Spongy bone lies within it beneath an outer compact layer.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The medullary cavity is an individual osteocyte space.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: The medullary cavity lies within the diaphysis. It contains marrow rather than an individual osteocyte.
rubric: The medullary cavity lies within the diaphysis.
It contains marrow rather than an individual osteocyte.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Compact bone contains no vessels or living cells.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Compact bone provides a dense outer structure. Its osteons organize vessels, matrix, and cells.
rubric: Compact bone provides a dense outer structure.
Its osteons organize vessels, matrix, and cells.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Spongy bone is made of empty holes with no matrix or cells.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Spongy bone is organized into trabeculae. Their arrangement helps bone accommodate stress without being a solid dense mass.
rubric: Spongy bone is organized into trabeculae.
Their arrangement helps bone accommodate stress without being a solid dense mass.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “An osteon is another name for the entire marrow cavity.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: An osteon consists of concentric lamellae around a central canal. The central canal carries vessels and nerves.
rubric: An osteon consists of concentric lamellae around a central canal.
The central canal carries vessels and nerves.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Endochondral ossification forms bone directly in a membrane without cartilage.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Endochondral ossification replaces a cartilage model with bone. A related cartilage-to-bone transition also occurs in fracture calli.
rubric: Endochondral ossification replaces a cartilage model with bone.
A related cartilage-to-bone transition also occurs in fracture calli.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “All bone formation must begin with a cartilage model.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Intramembranous ossification begins in a connective-tissue membrane. It does not require a hyaline cartilage model.
rubric: Intramembranous ossification begins in a connective-tissue membrane.
It does not require a hyaline cartilage model.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “An epiphyseal line is an active cartilage growth plate.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: The epiphyseal plate contains growth cartilage. Its activity supports longitudinal growth before closure.
rubric: The epiphyseal plate contains growth cartilage.
Its activity supports longitudinal growth before closure.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Appositional growth means increasing length only at a growth plate.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Appositional growth adds bone at the outer surface. Endosteal resorption enlarges the medullary cavity as the shaft thickens.
rubric: Appositional growth adds bone at the outer surface.
Endosteal resorption enlarges the medullary cavity as the shaft thickens.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The skeleton cannot store calcium once bone has formed.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: The skeleton stores minerals including calcium. Bone can release stored calcium when regulation requires it.
rubric: The skeleton stores minerals including calcium.
Bone can release stored calcium when regulation requires it.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Yellow marrow fat storage and red marrow blood-cell production are identical functions.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Red marrow produces blood cells through hematopoiesis. This function differs from forming bone matrix or storing fat.
rubric: Red marrow produces blood cells through hematopoiesis.
This function differs from forming bone matrix or storing fat.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Removing mechanical stress always strengthens bone.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Mechanical stress stimulates deposition of mineral salts and collagen fibers. Bone changes its structure in response to loading.
rubric: Mechanical stress stimulates deposition of mineral salts and collagen fibers.
Bone changes its structure in response to loading.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Low gravity increases ordinary weight-bearing stress on bone.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Reduced mechanical stress decreases the stimulus for bone maintenance. Bone can lose mineral salts and collagen fibers when unloaded.
rubric: Reduced mechanical stress decreases the stimulus for bone maintenance.
Bone can lose mineral salts and collagen fibers when unloaded.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Taking calcium makes vitamin D irrelevant to calcium absorption.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Vitamin D supports calcium absorption from the digestive tract. Calcium intake and absorption both matter for bone mineralization.
rubric: Vitamin D supports calcium absorption from the digestive tract.
Calcium intake and absorption both matter for bone mineralization.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Vitamin K is a type of bone-resorbing cell.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Vitamin K supports bone mineralization. The chapter describes possible cooperation with vitamin D in bone regulation.
rubric: Vitamin K supports bone mineralization.
The chapter describes possible cooperation with vitamin D in bone regulation.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “A reduction in bone mass always increases fracture resistance.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Osteoporosis involves reduced bone mass and weaker skeletal structure. Reduced strength increases fracture susceptibility.
rubric: Osteoporosis involves reduced bone mass and weaker skeletal structure.
Reduced strength increases fracture susceptibility.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Bone strength depends only on mineral and never on collagen.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Osteogenesis imperfecta affects collagen and bone strength. The matrix defect helps explain susceptibility to fractures.
rubric: Osteogenesis imperfecta affects collagen and bone strength.
The matrix defect helps explain susceptibility to fractures.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Calcitriol and calcitonin are two names for the same hormone.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Calcitriol is the active vitamin D hormone. It promotes intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate.
rubric: Calcitriol is the active vitamin D hormone.
It promotes intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Low blood calcium normally triggers the calcitonin pathway described for high calcium.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Low blood calcium promotes parathyroid hormone release. Its effects help raise blood calcium through bone, kidneys, and vitamin D pathways.
rubric: Low blood calcium promotes parathyroid hormone release.
Its effects help raise blood calcium through bone, kidneys, and vitamin D pathways.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Calcitonin stimulates the same low-calcium bone-resorption pathway as PTH.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast activity and promotes calcium uptake by bone. The chapter describes these effects as lowering blood calcium.
rubric: Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast activity and promotes calcium uptake by bone.
The chapter describes these effects as lowering blood calcium.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “PTH raises blood calcium by forcing the kidneys to discard all calcium.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: PTH promotes reabsorption of calcium by kidney tubules. Returning calcium from the filtrate helps conserve it in the blood.
rubric: PTH promotes reabsorption of calcium by kidney tubules.
Returning calcium from the filtrate helps conserve it in the blood.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “The PTH response must continue at full strength after blood calcium returns to normal.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Restored calcium binds receptors involved in the parathyroid response. The corrective response subsides once the regulated level is restored.
rubric: Restored calcium binds receptors involved in the parathyroid response.
The corrective response subsides once the regulated level is restored.

written.prompt: A learner writes: “Calcium has no physiological role outside bone.” Explain the correction using the relevant anatomy.
written.explanation: Calcium supports functions beyond skeletal mineralization. Its roles in muscle, nerves, and coagulation make blood-level regulation important.
rubric: Calcium supports functions beyond skeletal mineralization.
Its roles in muscle, nerves, and coagulation make blood-level regulation important.
